problem: Graph-based VLN-CE models (ETPNav-style topological planners) have not exploited large-scale, multi-dataset pretraining or reinforcement fine-tuning, while LVLM-based agents use these paradigms but are inefficient (redundant tokens, forward-view only, low-level actions).
motivation: The waypoint-based action space of graph planners is compact and well suited to efficient closed-loop RL. Existing speaker-generated pretraining instructions are stylistically monotonous and hallucinated, and R2R/RxR are trained in isolation. LVLM RFT is open-loop (single-turn outputs), whereas a graph agent can be optimized along a whole trajectory.
key_idea: Scale a graph-based VLN-CE planner with Gemini-re-annotated data and joint R2R+RxR pretraining, then apply online closed-loop GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning with episode-level outcome rewards.
insight: Pretraining quality strongly correlates with final online performance. Gemini-annotated data (R2R+G vs R2R+P) gives about +3% final score, stacking both synthetic sets gives +6.55% over R2R+G, and adding RxR data gives a smaller +1.16%. For GRPO, keeping dropout (in sampling and in frozen layers) and strict on-policy updates (mu=1) matter, while temperature scaling for diversity fails (ablation total 117.26 vs 121.18), likely because it only sharpens logits.
method: Gemini data annotation: re-annotate Prevalent trajectories with Gemini 2.0 Flash from stitched left/front/right views with a red arrow toward the next node; trajectory segmentation (1/2/3 splits) yields 6 instructions per call, no few-shot prompts, 10-25 words per subtask; ~2% of trajectories are discarded; average length grows from 31 to 48 words (Prevalent_Gemini_Aug).

Model (DPFT): text encoder (RoBERTa-style, 12 layers) plus node encoder (CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB, ResNet-50 depth, 2-layer panorama encoder) with task embeddings (R2R/RxR/Gemini); Symmetric Cross-Modal Fusion with 4 layers of unshared bidirectional cross-attention, then Text-Guided Graph Refinement (graph queries text, concatenated with the graph features).
Task heads: SAP head scores graph nodes (including STOP) for the next subgoal, and an MLM head is used in pretraining; the ETPNav topological mapping, waypoint predictor and controller are reused.

Offline joint pretraining: Prevalent 1M, Prevalent_Gemini_Aug 1M, RxR-Marky 1M, R2R_train 14K, RxR_train 80K, with SAP:MLM at 1:1; the checkpoint is chosen on the summed R2R+RxR val-unseen accuracies.
Online SFT: DAgger with expert actions from a global planner (mixing probability p), trained separately for R2R-CE and RxR-CE on 90% of the data.

Online RFT (GRPO): group size G=8 trajectories per episode, outcome reward (R2R: success indicator + SPL - d_final/6; RxR: nDTW + SDTW + gSPL - d_final/6), group-normalized advantage shared across all steps, clip 0.2, KL weight 0.04, on the remaining 10% of the data; only DPFT and SAP are tuned, dropout stays on, and there is one update per batch.

setting.backbone: ETP-R1 graph planner: RoBERTa-style text encoder + CLIP ViT-B/32 (frozen) + ResNet-50 depth (frozen) + DPFT transformer (trained)
setting.training_data: Pretraining: Prevalent 1M, Gemini-re-annotated Prevalent 1M, RxR-Marky 1M, R2R_train 14K, RxR_train 80K; then online DAgger SFT on 90% of R2R-CE/RxR-CE train and GRPO RFT on the other 10%
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views) building an online topological graph
setting.action_space: high-level waypoint/node selection on the topological graph, executed by a low-level controller (MOVE FORWARD 0.25m, TURN 15°, STOP)
setting.privileged: none at test time (a global planner gives expert actions only during DAgger training)

numbers_note: The R2R-CE Val Unseen ablation table (Ours-GRPO SR 65.36 / SPL 55.82) differs slightly from the main table entries; only the main table is listed. RxR-CE test results are not reported.
results: Ours-GRPO sets a new SOTA on R2R-CE val-unseen (SR 65, SPL 56, NE 3.94) and test-unseen (SR 64, SPL 54, NE 4.19), beating G3D-LF (test SR 58, SPL 51) by +6 SR and +3 SPL. On RxR-CE val-unseen it reaches nDTW 65.31 and SDTW 50.41 versus HNR's 63.56 and 47.24. The DAgger-only model already beats prior methods, and GRPO adds roughly 2% SR/SPL on top.
limitations: RFT uses only 10% of the training data and the ablations are mostly on R2R-CE; there is no real-robot evaluation.
Depends on the ETPNav waypoint predictor and a pretrained topological pipeline, and needs the Gemini API to generate data.
RxR-CE test-unseen results are not reported, and the paper gives no comparison against LVLM-based agents.
